messages:
viv: Heads up 1: we need to pick a canonical pattern for private customer connectivity when the control plane is split (central control plane + regional dataplane). Options on the table: per-tenant VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints, or a lightweight ENI-based proxy. Each has routing, IP-preservation, and ops implications. Thoughts?

alex: Quick summary from infra POV: Peering = easiest path-preserving (no SNAT) but scales poorly (route table explosion & cross-account peering limits). PrivateLink = scales nicely but we NAT at the endpoint (loses src ip) unless we do proxy-preserve mapping. ENI proxy (attach ENI in customer VPC & NAT-less hairpin) preserves src ip but requires privileges in each account and is heavy.

jay: Also consider control-plane separation lifecycle: when CP is central, dataplane agents in customer VPC need bootstrap tokens. For peering we only need a route and security-group handshake. For PrivateLink we need NLB + target provisioning and cross-account acceptance. Operational surface grows.

tara: SLO/SLAs angle: customers with pinned IPs expect stable source IP. PrivateLink will break pinned-IP assumptions unless we offer NAT translation mapping or Elastic IP forwarder in the middle.

alex: For NAT mapping approach we prototyped a header mapping in the proxy: preserve original IP in X-Forwarded-For and maintain ephemeral mapping table. But downstream services that validate src IP (e.g., customer firewalls) can still reject.

jay: Another idea: use per-tenant route tables + proxy nodes in the customer's account that we manage as a tiny agent (ENI attach + iptables). That keeps IPs native and gives us local NAT control but increases blast radius and onboarding complexity.

viv: Could we combine PrivateLink for scale and an optional 'preserve-ip bridge' for customers that require IP stability (paid addon)? So default = PrivateLink, paid = ENI-agent.

tara: Sounds reasonable. Need to list exact tradeoffs for sales: cost delta, time-to-onboard, required IAM roles, failure modes. Also what does split control plane mean for certificate rotation and cert trust boundaries?

alex: Certs: central CP holds CA for control plane TLS. Agents in customer VPC use short-lived certs from CP for mTLS. Data path TLS (client->endpoint) unchanged. For PrivateLink we terminate TLS at our NLB unless we SNI passthrough (possible but loses visibility for L7 features). We should document both.

jay: Failure modes to call out: - Peering: route table corruption / accidental route leak - PrivateLink: cross-account acceptance failure / NLB AZ imbalance - ENI-agent: agent crash + ENI detach race causing blackhole

viv: For cutover/playbook we need a low-risk onboarding path and emergency rollback. Proposal: 1) default onboarding via PrivateLink (self-serve) with sampled traffic mirroring to canary route; 2) if tenant buys preserve-ip, schedule agent install window and do ENI attach during maintenance; 3) emergency rollback = withdraw endpoint & BGP/route revert to previous state.

tara: Add step: when enabling preserve-ip agent, run a small traffic validation (TCP handshake + signed token exchange) to confirm no midstream NAT. Command we use in spike: 

# from orchestration host
ssh agent@customer-proxy \
  "ip link show eth0 && sudo iptables -t nat -L -n"

if iptables shows MASQUERADE on POSTROUTING -> fail install.

alex: Also recommend guardrails: automated IAM least-privilege template, cloudwatch/alarm export to our monitoring, and an uninstall hook that returns ENI + security groups to original owner.

jay: Metric checklist for rollout: route convergence time, % of flows preserving src ip, TCP reset rate post-cutover, control-plane auth latency. We set thresholds before turning on auto-cutover.

ops-bot: Note: there is an open spike ticket PI-345 that contains perf numbers for ENI-attach times across regions. See https://go/PI-345 (internal).

viv: Action items: - viv: draft the onboarding matrix (privatelink default vs preserve-ip addon) - alex: IAM + operator automation template - jay: perf & alerting SLOs doc - tara: failure-mode runbook + rollback commands. I'll assemble a single cutover-playbook doc once drafts are in.

alex: One more small incantation for route prep: when moving from PrivateLink -> ENI preserve mode, prep local control-plane routes with a lower preference so we can test traffic steering: 

# create test route in customer route table
sudo aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-12345 --destination-cidr-block 10.0.0.0/16 --instance-id i-test --dry-run

use dry-run to validate permissions first.

viv: Cool. Thanks everyone. If anyone has customers with hard constraints around cross-account agents (legal/regulatory), ping me privately before we finalize the template.
